rationale: Comprehensive evaluation of available clinical cohorts confirms that optic atrophy and retinal degeneration are near-completely penetrant ocular manifestations of biallelic pathogenic FDXR variants, particularly in ophthalmologically ascertained cohorts (such as 11/11 patients in Yi et al. 2023 displaying complete optic disc pallor and generalized retinal degeneration). In contrast, auditory neuropathy demonstrates variable age of onset, incomplete penetrance, or delayed clinical presentation, particularly when patients initially present to ophthalmic clinics with early-onset retinal dystrophy or optic atrophy. Conversely, when ascertained through audiology clinics, patients demonstrate auditory neuropathy with variable or evolving systemic and visual involvement, confirming that normal auditory electrophysiology does not exclude FDXR deficiency in early-stage visual presentations.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 11 unrelated patients with biallelic FDXR variants ascertained from an inherited eye disease registry, 100% (11/11) presented with complete optic disc pallor, severe attenuation of retinal vessels, and generalized retinal degeneration, presenting as Leber congenital amaurosis (4/11) or early-onset severe retinal dystrophy (7/11).

source.quote: Biallelic pathogenic or likely pathogenic FDXR variants were identified in 11 unrelated patients... Fundus observation showed complete optic disc pallor, silver wiring or severe attenuation of retinal vessels, and varying degrees of generalized retinal degeneration.

evidence.text: Initial characterization of FDXR-associated disease identified biallelic variants causing auditory neuropathy and optic atrophy across 8 affected individuals from 4 independent families, establishing the classic sensorial neuropathy phenotype.

source.title: FDXR mutations cause sensorial neuropathies and expand the spectrum of mitochondrial Fe-S-synthesis diseases
source.journal: The American Journal of Human Genetics
source.quote: Here, we report on eight subjects from four independent families affected by auditory neuropathy and optic atrophy. Whole-exome sequencing revealed biallelic mutations in FDXR in affected subjects of each family.

evidence.text: Systematic evaluation of non-isolated auditory neuropathy identified FDXR variants in patients presenting primarily with auditory neuropathy whose onset of hearing loss ranged widely from 2 to 25 years (mean 11 years), with 71.4% presenting additional neurologic and systemic features.

source.title: Identification of genetic mechanisms of non-isolated auditory neuropathy with various phenotypes in Chinese families
source.quote: Patients' age of hearing loss onset ranged from 2 to 25 years, averaging 11 years. Hearing loss varied from mild to profound, with 57.1%(4/7) of patients having risk factors and 71.4%(5/7) exhibiting additional systemic symptoms such as muscle weakness, ataxia, and high arches.

evidence.text: Report of a patient with biallelic FDXR mutations demonstrating prominent optic atrophy alongside progressive neurological manifestations (ataxia, peripheral neuropathy), highlighting consistent optic nerve vulnerability.

evidence.text: Case report illustrating a young female patient with novel compound heterozygous FDXR variants exhibiting severe optic atrophy with marked thinning of the bilateral retinal nerve fiber layer.

new_directions.question_text: What is the longitudinal incidence and median age of onset of auditory neuropathy in patients with FDXR mutations who initially present with isolated early-onset retinal dystrophy or optic atrophy?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying the temporal kinetics of cochlear/auditory nerve deterioration in ophthalmic-first cases will establish surveillance intervals for early audiologic intervention.

new_directions.question_text: Does residual ferredoxin reductase enzyme activity or specific domain localization correlate with the severity and penetrance of retinal versus cochlear neuroepithelial degeneration?
new_directions.rationale: Elucidating genotype-phenotype correlations could explain why certain missense alleles present predominantly with childhood Leber congenital amaurosis-like phenotypes while others present with later-onset auditory neuropathy.
